nodes.title: Async I/O Engine and Group Commit
nodes.description: Covers the pluggable I/O backend system (Mmap, Pread, IoUring), ExtentList coalescing, io_uring capability gating, async read engine with inline fast-path, and async write engine with group commit for DurabilityMode::Strict.
nodes.body:
# Async I/O Engine and Group Commit

OIFS separates metadata operations from payload data reading. Filesystem metadata (superblocks, bitmaps, inodes, indirect pointer blocks, and directory indices) resides on the shared `MAP_SHARED` memory map for zero-copy, low-overhead access. File payloads can be large, cold, and scattered across physical blocks—reading them through the mmap means every uncached page is a synchronous page fault, one fault at a time.

P3.2 introduced a pluggable data-block read engine (`src/io_engine.rs`) that decouples physical payload I/O from memory-mapped page faults, enabling applications to select between three backends: **Mmap**, **Pread**, and **IoUring**. In v1.4.0 the async write pipeline adds a dedicated group-commit thread that merges concurrent `DurabilityMode::Strict` operations behind a single `flush()` barrier.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    subgraph ReadPath ["DiskManager::read_at / read_at_batch"]
        Guard["Acquire Read Lock (inner.read())"]
        Prepare["read_at_prepare: Block Traversal + Extent Coalescing"]
        Extents["ExtentList (Contiguous Disk + Buffer Range Merge)"]
        Select{"IoBackend Selection"}
    end

    subgraph MmapPath ["Mmap (Default)"]
        MmapRead["read_mmap: memcpy from mmap slice"]
    end

    subgraph PreadPath ["Pread"]
        PreadLoop["read_pread: file.read_exact_at per extent"]
    end

    subgraph UringPath ["IoUring (Linux 5.15+ / RHEL 9.3+)"]
        Checkout["RingPool::checkout (64-entry ring)"]
        Populate["Populate SQEs (split >1MiB extents)"]
        Submit["submit_and_wait(1)"]
        Reap["Reap CQEs, handle short reads / transient errors"]
        Checkin["RingPool::checkin (cache up to 16)"]
    end

    Guard --> Prepare --> Extents --> Select
    Select -->|Mmap| MmapRead
    Select -->|Pread| PreadLoop
    Select -->|IoUring| Checkout --> Populate --> Submit --> Reap --> Checkin

    style MmapPath fill:#e8f5e9,stroke:#2e7d32
    style PreadPath fill:#fff3e0,stroke:#ef6c00
    style UringPath fill:#e3f2fd,stroke:#1565c0
```

---

## 1. IoBackend Architecture and Selection

The `IoBackend` enum defines three distinct data-block retrieval strategies ([src/io_engine.rs#L36-L51](repo://src/io_engine.rs#L36-L51)):

| Backend | Value | Mechanism | Platforms |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `IoBackend::Mmap` (Default) | 0 | `memcpy` directly from the shared memory mapping | All |
| `IoBackend::Pread` | 1 | Positional `pread(2)` syscall per coalesced extent | All Unix |
| `IoBackend::IoUring` | 2 | Batched async submission to a pooled `io_uring` ring | Linux ≥ 5.6, `io_uring` cargo feature |

All backends read through the standard OS page cache without `O_DIRECT`, ensuring that recently written dirty pages (including uncommitted mutations under `DurabilityMode::Lazy`) are immediately visible across all backends ([src/io_engine.rs#L1-L25](repo://src/io_engine.rs#L1-L25)).

Backend selection is configurable via:

- **Environment variable**: `OIFS_IO_BACKEND=mmap|pread|io_uring` (case-insensitive; aliases: `uring`, `iouring`, `io-uring`). Read once at `DiskManager` construction via `IoBackend::from_env()` ([src/io_engine.rs#L34-L35](repo://src/io_engine.rs#L34-L35)).
- **Programmatic Rust API**: `DiskManager::set_io_backend(backend)` or builder-style `DiskManager::with_io_backend(backend)` ([src/disk.rs#L1615-L1624](repo://src/disk.rs#L1615-L1624)).
- **FFI**: `oifs_set_io_backend(handle, backend_u8)` and `oifs_get_io_backend(handle)` ([src/ffi.rs#L726-L755](repo://src/ffi.rs#L726-L755)).

```rust
// Querying and configuring the backend
let dm = DiskManager::open("data.oifs", 10 * 1024 * 1024)?;
let effective = dm.set_io_backend(IoBackend::IoUring);
assert_eq!(dm.io_backend(), effective);        // effective backend after gating
assert_eq!(dm.requested_io_backend(), IoBackend::IoUring); // what was asked for
```

Requesting `IoUring` where it is unavailable never fails; `IoBackend::resolve()` transparently falls back to `Pread`, and the effective backend is reported separately from the requested one ([src/io_engine.rs#L60-L68](repo://src/io_engine.rs#L60-L68)).

---

## 2. ExtentList Block Coalescing

Non-contiguous files incur high syscall or SQE overhead if dispatched one 4 KiB block at a time. OIFS solves this through `ExtentList`, which merges contiguous physical disk runs **and** destination buffer offsets on `push` ([src/io_engine.rs#L232-L287](repo://src/io_engine.rs#L232-L287)):

```rust
pub fn push(&mut self, disk_offset: u64, buf_offset: usize, len: usize) {
    if len == 0 { return; }
    if let Some(last) = self.extents.last_mut()
        && last.disk_offset.checked_add(last.len as u64) == Some(disk_offset)
        && last.buf_offset.checked_add(last.len) == Some(buf_offset)
        && let Some(new_len) = last.len.checked_add(len)
    {
        last.len = new_len;          // merge into previous extent
        return;
    }
    self.extents.push(ReadExtent {
        disk_offset,
        buf_offset,
        len,
    });
}
```

A file whose blocks were allocated contiguously therefore collapses into a single extent—i.e., a single `pread` / single SQE regardless of its size in blocks. This applies to both `read_at` and `read_at_batch` paths.

---

## 3. io_uring Capability Gating

The `IoUring` backend is not available everywhere. The engine performs a one-time, cached probe at first `IoEngine` construction ([src/io_engine.rs#L497-L502](repo://src/io_engine.rs#L497-L502)) and rejects `IoUring` when any of the following conditions hold:

| Condition | Details |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Non-Linux** | `io_uring` is a Linux-only interface. |
| **Cargo feature disabled** | The `io_uring` feature must be enabled at compile time. |
| **Kernel too old** | Mainline Linux ≥ 5.15 required (via `MIN_RECOMMENDED_KERNEL = (5, 15)`) ([src/io_engine.rs#L115](repo://src/io_engine.rs#L115)). |
| **RHEL 9 backport missing** | RHEL 9.0–9.2 shipped with `CONFIG_IO_URING=n`. RHEL 9.3+ (kernel `5.14.0-362+`, build ≥ 362 on `.el9` kernels) backports `io_uring` as a Technology Preview ([src/io_engine.rs#L118-L128](repo://src/io_engine.rs#L118-L128)). |
| **Sysctl disabled** | RHEL 9.4+ adds `kernel.io_uring_disabled` (0 = allow all, 1 = privileged/group only, 2 = disabled). If the sysctl blocks ring creation, the probe fails and the engine falls back to `Pread`. |
| **seccomp / container** | The `io_uring_enter(2)` syscall may be filtered; the probe catches `EPERM`/`EACCES` as unsupported. |
| **Kernel lacks `IORING_OP_READ`** | The probe registers a `Probe` and verifies `opcode::Read::CODE` is supported ([src/io_engine.rs#L535-L537](repo://src/io_engine.rs#L535-L537)). |

The `OIFS_ALLOW_PRE_5_15` environment variable bypasses the kernel-version gate (but not the probe) for testing on older kernels.

---

## 4. Async Read Engine: Inline Fast-Path + Background Pool

The Rust API exposes `DiskManager::read_at_async`, `read_data_async`, and `read_at_batch_async`, all returning `OifsAsyncTask<T>` ([src/disk.rs#L9231-L9249](repo://src/disk.rs#L9231-L9249)). The FFI layer provides `oifs_read_at_async`, `oifs_read_at_async_cb`, and corresponding futures ([src/ffi.rs#L1583-L1880](repo://src/ffi.rs#L1583-L1880)).

### Inline Fast-Path (Zero Thread Hop)

When the read can be satisfied entirely from cached data, the operation completes synchronously on the calling thread:

- **Mmap hits**: The requested range is raw, uncompressed, unencrypted, and the backing is `StorageMode::Mmap`.
- **DataPageCache hits**: `StorageMode::FileIo` with the range resident in the internal page cache (≤ 16 MiB per extent).
- **ChunkReadCache hits**: Seekable 64K chunked files where the single target chunk is cached.
- **DecodedBlobCache hits**: Compressed/encrypted files (≤ 16 MiB total) with a decoded blob already cached.

The fast-path is implemented in `try_read_at_inline_into` ([src/disk.rs#L9015-L9170](repo://src/disk.rs#L9015-L9170)). On success, `OifsAsyncTask::ready` returns an immediately resolved future—no heap allocation, no background thread wake-up.

### Background Pool Dispatch

On cache miss, lock contention, or cold decode (compressed/encrypted files exceeding cache limits), the read is submitted to a persistent background thread pool via `OifsAsyncTask::spawn`. The pool uses a bounded queue with a condition variable; workers execute the full `read_at` path including indirect block traversal, decompression, decryption, and filter unapplication.

---

## 5. Async Write Engine: Group Commit for Strict Durability

Writes under `DurabilityMode::Strict` require a durable `flush()` (metadata + payload `msync`) after every mutation. To avoid serializing flushes when many writers operate concurrently, OIFS v1.4.0 introduces a **group-commit** thread that batches multiple operations behind a single barrier.

### Architecture

1. **Submission**: Async write APIs (`create_file_with_data_async`, `write_data_async`, and FFI equivalents `oifs_create_file_with_data_async`, `oifs_write_file_async`) call `submit_group_write_op` ([src/disk.rs#L8830](repo://src/disk.rs#L8830)), which enqueues a `GroupWriteOp` containing:
   - A cloned `DiskManager` (Arc).
   - The closure to execute under the write lock (`run`).
   - A completion callback (`complete`).

2. **Single Worker Thread**: A dedicated thread named `"oifs-group-commit"` ([src/disk.rs#L8835-L8845](repo://src/disk.rs#L8835-L8845)) wakes on the condition variable, drains up to 128 ops from the queue, and processes them in a batch.

3. **Deferred Strict Sync**: Inside the batch, a thread-local guard `DeferStrictSyncGuard::enter()` ([src/disk.rs#L8538-L8547](repo://src/disk.rs#L8538-L8547)) sets a flag that causes `DiskManager::flush` (invoked internally by strict write paths) to **defer** its `msync` and return immediately.

4. **Execution Phase**: Each operation’s `run` closure executes under the exclusive write lock sequentially (one at a time to preserve ACID ordering). The `run` closures may include multiple internal `flush()` calls that become no-ops while the guard is active.

5. **Harvest Window**: While the batch is running, newly arriving ops are appended up to the 128-op limit ([src/disk.rs#L8873-L8883](repo://src/disk.rs#L8873-L8883)).

6. **Group Flush**: After all `run` closures complete, the guard drops, the thread iterates over the **unique** `DiskManager` inner pointers that participated, and issues one `flush()` per distinct manager ([src/disk.rs#L8885-L8895](repo://src/disk.rs#L8885-L8895)).

7. **Completion**: Each operation’s `complete` callback is invoked with the result (or the group-flush error if its manager was in the strict set) ([src/disk.rs#L8897-L8905](repo://src/disk.rs#L8897-L8905)).

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant C1 as Caller 1 (Strict)
    participant C2 as Caller 2 (Strict)
    participant Q as GroupWriteQueue
    participant W as Worker Thread
    participant DM1 as DiskManager A
    participant DM2 as DiskManager B

    C1->>Q: submit_group_write_op(op1)
    C2->>Q: submit_group_write_op(op2)
    Q->>W: notify_one
    W->>Q: drain batch [op1, op2]
    W->>W: DeferStrictSyncGuard::enter()
    W->>DM1: op1.run() (flush becomes no-op)
    W->>DM2: op2.run() (flush becomes no-op)
    W->>W: DeferStrictSyncGuard drops
    W->>DM1: flush()  (single msync)
    W->>DM2: flush()  (single msync)
    W->>C1: complete(op1_result)
    W->>C2: complete(op2_result)
```

### Effect

If 100 concurrent threads call `write_data_async` with `DurabilityMode::Strict` on the same filesystem, they incur **one** `msync` instead of 100. Latency scales with the slowest operation in the batch, not the sum.

### Other Durability Modes

- `RangeAsync`: Uses the existing `PendingAsyncRanges` accumulator + `async_drain_ready` flag; no group-commit thread involvement.
- `LegacyWholeMmapAsync`: Defers to the legacy whole-mmap async path.
- `Lazy`: No implicit sync; caller controls durability explicitly.

---

## 6. FFI Async Surface: OIFSAsyncFuture, Polling, Callbacks

The FFI layer wraps `OifsAsyncTask` into `OIFSAsyncFuture` ([src/ffi.rs#L1586](repo://src/ffi.rs#L1586)), adding a drop barrier that waits for background reads still writing into caller buffers.

### Future-based API

| Function | Purpose |
| :--- | :--- |
| `oifs_read_at_async` | Async positional read; inline fast-path returns immediately ready future. |
| `oifs_create_file_with_data_async` | Async file create + write via group-commit pipeline. |
| `oifs_write_file_async` | Async file write via group-commit pipeline. |
| `oifs_flush_async` | Async flush on background pool. |

All return `*mut OIFSAsyncFuture` (or null on invalid args). The future owns the task; callers **must** eventually call `oifs_async_free`.

### Poll / Wait / Error

```c
int oifs_async_poll(const OIFSAsyncFuture* fut);    // 1=ready, 0=pending, -1=invalid
int64_t oifs_async_wait(OIFSAsyncFuture* fut);      // blocks, returns result or -1
int oifs_async_last_error(const OIFSAsyncFuture* fut, char* buf, uint32_t buf_size);
void oifs_async_free(OIFSAsyncFuture* fut);         // waits if background read in progress
```

### Callback-based API

For environments without polling infrastructure:

```c
typedef void (*OifsAsyncStatusCallback)(int64_t status, void* user_data);
typedef void (*OifsAsyncReadCallback)(int64_t status, const uint8_t* buf, uint64_t len, void* user_data);

int oifs_read_at_async_cb(... OifsAsyncReadCallback cb, void* user_data);
int oifs_create_file_with_data_async_cb(... OifsAsyncStatusCallback cb, void* user_data);
int oifs_write_file_async_cb(... OifsAsyncStatusCallback cb, void* user_data);
```

Callbacks execute on the background pool thread; they must not block.

---

## 7. Configuration Summary

| Setting | Mechanism | Default |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Read backend** | `OIFS_IO_BACKEND=mmap\|pread\|io_uring` | `mmap` |
| **Kernel version gate bypass** | `OIFS_ALLOW_PRE_5_15=1` | Enforced |
| **Durability** | `DiskManager::set_durability_mode(Strict \| RangeAsync \| LegacyWholeMmapAsync \| Lazy)` | `Lazy` |
| **Max cached extent** | `MAX_CACHED_EXTENT = 16 MiB` (inline fast-path threshold) | Constant |

---

## 8. Invariants and Failure Semantics

- **io_uring fallback is silent**: `IoBackend::IoUring` requested → unsupported → `effective()` returns `Pread`; no error is raised.
- **ExtentList never wraps**: `checked_add` guards against integer overflow; a run that would overflow `usize` splits into a new extent ([src/io_engine.rs#L242-L247](repo://src/io_engine.rs#L242-L247)).
- **Background reads never UAF**: `OIFSAsyncFuture`’s `wait_on_drop=true` forces `oifs_async_free` to block until the background read finishes writing into the caller’s buffer.
- **Group commit is per-DiskManager**: Two distinct `DiskManager` instances (different image files) each get their own flush barrier; the worker deduplicates by `Arc::as_ptr(&dm.inner)`.
- **Strict writes in group commit are atomic w.r.t durability**: If the group flush fails, every strict op in the batch surfaces the same I/O error via its completion callback.
- **Inline fast-path is best-effort**: Any lock contention, cache miss, or decode requirement falls back to the background pool without surfacing an error to the caller.

---

## 9. Related Pages

- [DiskManager & Persistence](disk_manager_and_persistence.md) — Core storage manager, durability modes, write pipeline
- [FFI Interface](ffi_interface.md) — Complete FFI surface including async APIs
- [Testing & Verification](../operations/testing_and_verification.md) — Kani proofs for kernel version gating, extent coalescing, backend agreement
- [FFI Workflow](../workflows/ffi_workflow.md) — Example async read/write patterns from C/C++

nodes.title: Block & Inode Allocation
nodes.description: Documents the sequential hint-based block and inode allocator (SimpleBlockAllocator), multi-block bitmap layout (v3), hardware-accelerated tzcnt scanning, BitmapSliceMut write-through mirrors for FileIo mode, and allocation rollback on WAL failure.
nodes.body:
## Responsibility and ownership

Block and inode allocation is centralized in `SimpleBlockAllocator` (`src/allocator.rs`) operating on 4 KB bitmap slices. The `DiskManagerInner` (`src/disk.rs`) owns the actual bitmap slices in the mmapped image (or in-memory mirrors under `FileIo` mode) and drives allocation through cached search hints stored in `free_block_hint` and `free_inode_hint`. Every allocation, deallocation, directory write, and indirect-block expansion on the write path goes through this machinery, so it is the single authority over which physical blocks are free or in use.

For journaled images, allocation is first simulated against in-memory bitmap copies via `AllocSim` (`src/journal.rs`) before any on-disk metadata is mutated. `AllocSim` mirrors `SimpleBlockAllocator` semantics exactly (same hint handling, same "first free bit at or after hint" rule), so the IDs it predicts are the IDs the real allocator will hand out when the transaction is applied.

## On-disk bitmap representation (v3 multi-block layout)

A bitmap is a flat bit array stored in one or more 4 KB blocks. Bit `0` means free and bit `1` means allocated. `SuperBlock` (`src/superblock.rs`) records where each bitmap lives and how many blocks each spans:

- Inode bitmap starts at `inode_bitmap_block` (block 1 in legacy layout; spans `inode_bitmap_blocks()` blocks in v3), tracking inodes from ID 0.
- Data bitmap starts at `data_bitmap_block` (block 2 in legacy; spans `data_bitmap_blocks()` blocks in v3), tracking data blocks starting at `data_block_start`.

The v3 layout computes `inode_bitmap_blocks = inode_count.div_ceil(BITMAP_BLOCK_BITS).max(1)` and `data_bitmap_blocks` derived from the recorded `data_block_start` and `inode_table_block` offsets. Bit index mapping: for the data bitmap, the bit index for a given `block_id` is `block_id - data_block_start`. The inode bitmap uses a direct 0-based index (inode ID == bit index).

Two views wrap the raw bytes:

- `BitmapRef` (`src/bitmap.rs`) — read-only view used for analysis, scanning, and fsck.
- `Bitmap` (`src/bitmap.rs`) — mutable view that forwards `set`/`clear` and delegates search helpers to a `BitmapRef`.

Under `StorageMode::FileIo`, the on-disk bitmaps are mirrored in memory (`FileBacking.inode_bitmap` / `data_bitmap` in `src/storage.rs`). Mutable access is provided through `BitmapSliceMut` (see below).

## 64-bit word scanning and hardware `tzcnt`

The bitmap deliberately processes 64 bits (8 bytes) per CPU word instead of bit by bit. The key operations in `BitmapRef` all use `chunks_exact(8)`:

- `find_first_free_from` masks out bits before the search start with `(1u64 << bit_in_chunk) - 1`, then locates the first zero bit using `(!masked_word).trailing_zeros()` — a single hardware `tzcnt` instruction on x86/ARM.
- `for_each_set_bit` (used by fsck, defragmentation, and `analyze_fragmentation`) iterates set bits with `word &= word - 1` to clear the lowest set bit each cycle, yielding only as many iterations as there are allocated blocks.
- `analyze_fragmentation` (`src/disk.rs`) additionally special-cases whole words equal to `0` (all free) or `u64::MAX` (all used) so densely packed regions are scanned in constant time.

These optimizations deliver 11×–13.4× faster free-block scans and ~7.4× fsck speedup over bit-by-bit scanning.

## Allocation hints for amortized O(1) sequential allocation

Before hints, allocating many blocks sequentially re-scanned the bitmap from bit 0 every time, producing O(N²) behavior. `allocate_with_hint` (`src/allocator.rs`) accepts an optional hint block ID and translates it to a bit index (`hint - start_block_offset`) before calling `find_next_free_wrapped`.

`DiskManagerInner` keeps two hints and advances them after each allocation:

- `allocate_block` reads `free_block_hint`, allocates, then sets `free_block_hint = blk + 1`.
- Inode allocation in `create_entry_internal` reads `free_inode_hint`, allocates, then sets `free_inode_hint = new_inode_id + 1`.

When a hint points past the end of the bitmap, `find_next_free_wrapped` wraps around and searches from bit 0 for a bit below the hint, so allocation is guaranteed to find space whenever one exists. Freeing a block updates the hint downward (`min_freed_blk < free_block_hint`), keeping sequential allocation compact.

## Contiguous-run allocation for seekable 64K chunks

Seekable 64 KiB chunked files (`INODE_FLAG_SEEKABLE_64K`) require each chunk to occupy a contiguous run of physical blocks so that a chunk can be read with a single I/O operation. `SimpleBlockAllocator::allocate_contiguous` (`src/allocator.rs`) finds the first run of `count` consecutive free bits starting from a hint, using `BitmapRef::find_contiguous_free_wrapped`. The allocator scans 64-bit words and skips entirely used words in O(1), then checks candidate runs bit-by-bit only when a mixed word is encountered.

The write path (`commit_prepared_chunked_write` in `src/disk/chunked.rs`) stages through `AllocSim`:

1. For each chunk, `sim.alloc_contiguous(backing, prepared.blocks_needed)` reserves a contiguous run in the simulator's data-bitmap copy.
2. The run is recorded in the WAL via `SetDataBitmapRange { start_block, count, allocated: true }` (coalesced from individual `SetDataBitmap` ops).
3. Payload bytes are written into the newly allocated blocks in the mmap.
4. Old chunk blocks (if any) are freed via `sim.free_contiguous` and `SetDataBitmapRange { allocated: false }`.
5. The inode's chunk-entry pointer is updated to point at the new run (`sim_set_logical_chunk_entry` emits a `WriteBlockSlice` for the pointer table entry).

This guarantees that every seekable chunk maps to a single contiguous physical extent, eliminating intra-chunk seeks.

## BitmapSliceMut: write-through mirrors for FileIo mode

Under `StorageMode::FileIo` there is no mmap; the filesystem image is accessed via `pread`/`pwrite`. To keep bitmap mutations coherent, `DiskManagerInner` provides mutable access through `BitmapSliceMut` (`src/storage.rs`):

```rust
pub(crate) struct BitmapSliceMut<'a> {
    slice: &'a mut [u8],
    file_writeback: Option<(&'a File, u64)>,  // (file handle, file offset of bitmap start)
    dirty_range: Option<(usize, usize)>,     // narrowed byte range [start..end)
}
```

- `inode_bitmap_slice_mut()` and `data_bitmap_slice_mut()` on `ImageBacking` return a `BitmapSliceMut` borrowing the in-memory mirror.
- `DerefMut` allows direct byte mutation (`slice[byte] |= mask`).
- `set_dirty_range(byte_start, byte_end)` and `set_dirty_bits(start_bit, bit_count)` narrow the flush range.
- On `Drop`, `flush_writeback()` is called automatically: under `FileIo` it issues a `pwrite` of the dirty range to the bitmap's file offset; under `Mmap` it is a no-op (the mmap is already coherent).
- Explicit `flush_writeback()` is also available for callers that need synchronous persistence before the guard drops.

This design makes bitmap writes under `FileIo` as cheap as mmap writes (single `pwrite` of the modified span on drop) while guaranteeing the on-disk bitmap is updated before the mutating function returns.

## AllocSim: WAL-first allocation simulation

`AllocSim` (`src/journal.rs`) is an in-memory allocation simulator used exclusively by journaled code paths (`write_data_journaled`, `commit_prepared_chunked_write`, `truncate_chunked_64k`, `create_entry_journaled`). It mirrors `SimpleBlockAllocator` behavior exactly so that block IDs assigned during simulation are the same IDs the real allocator will produce when the transaction is applied.

Key design points:

- **Lazy data-bitmap copy**: `new_data_only` avoids copying the data bitmap until the first allocation or free actually happens, saving 4–64 KB memcpy on pure in-place overwrites.
- **Fresh-block tracking**: `fresh_blocks`, `fresh_set`, and `unzeroed_fresh` record blocks allocated during this transaction. When a fresh block is first written, `take_unzeroed_fresh` returns true so the caller can zero the slack bytes before writing payload.
- **Pointer simulation**: `pointers` map `(parent_block, entry_index) → child_block` records indirect-block pointer writes without touching the mmap. `sim_get_or_alloc_block` and `sim_child` use this to build the indirect tree in the WAL.
- **Hint synchronization**: On commit, `guard.free_block_hint = sim.free_block_hint` and `guard.free_inode_hint = sim.free_inode_hint` advance the real hints to match the simulated state.

Allocation operations against `AllocSim` emit `MetadataOp` entries that are later coalesced and written to the journal:

- Single block: `SetDataBitmap { block_id, allocated: true }`
- Contiguous run: `SetDataBitmapRange { start_block, count, allocated: true }` (after coalescing)
- Free: same ops with `allocated: false`

## Journal interaction: commit, apply, and allocation rollback

The journal encodes bitmap mutations as two operation types:

- `SetDataBitmap { block_id, allocated }` — single-bit set/clear.
- `SetDataBitmapRange { start_block, count, allocated }` — contiguous run set/clear.

`coalesce_ops` (`src/journal.rs`) merges adjacent `SetDataBitmap` ops of the same polarity into `SetDataBitmapRange`, shrinking WAL frame sizes for multi-block operations by orders of magnitude. The canonical phase order in a committed transaction is: `SetInodeBitmap` → `SetDataBitmapRange` → `WriteBlockSlice` → `WriteInode`. During replay, applying a `SetDataBitmap` or `SetDataBitmapRange` is strictly idempotent (Kani-verified), so redo is safe.

### Commit point and rollback on WAL failure

`commit_journal_tx` (`src/disk.rs`) is the **commit point**: it appends the transaction to the WAL ring buffer and calls `JournalRegionMut::flush_writeback()` to force the frame (and updated journal header) to stable storage. If `flush_writeback` fails:

```rust
if let Err(e) = region.flush_writeback() {
    region[..hdr_len].copy_from_slice(&prev_hdr[..hdr_len]); // restore old header
    return Err(e.into());
}
```

The previous journal header is restored in-memory, the error propagates up, and **the transaction is not applied**. Because the hints (`free_block_hint`, `free_inode_hint`) are only advanced *after* both `commit_journal_tx` and `apply_journal_ops` succeed (see `write_data_journaled`), a WAL flush failure leaves the hints unchanged — the simulated allocations in `AllocSim` are effectively discarded. This is the allocation rollback mechanism: the simulator's predicted block IDs are never committed to the real bitmap, and the allocator's hints do not advance, so a subsequent retry will allocate the same physical blocks again.

On success, `apply_journal_ops` mutates the in-memory bitmap (through `BitmapSliceMut` or mmap) and the block payloads. Under `FileIo`, the `BitmapSliceMut` guards created during `apply_journal_ops` will flush their dirty ranges on drop, persisting the bitmap updates.

## Indirect block addressing scheme

`DiskManager` maps logical file blocks to physical blocks using a hybrid direct + indirect index tree. Each block pointer entry is an 8-byte little-endian `u64`, so a 4 KB block holds 512 pointers.

| Level | Pointer field | Capacity | Logical block index range |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Direct | `blocks[0..10]` | 10 blocks | 0 – 9 |
| Single indirect | `blocks[10]` | 512 blocks | 10 – 521 |
| Double indirect | `blocks[11]` | 262,144 blocks | 522 – 262,665 |
| Triple indirect | `triple_indirect` | 134,217,728 blocks | 262,666 – 134,480,393 |

Total: 134,480,394 blocks × 4 KB ≈ 513 GB. Allocation walks the levels via `get_or_alloc_block` (`src/disk.rs`), lazily allocating intermediate sub-indirect blocks with `alloc_and_zero_block`. Reads and collection use hierarchical skipping: when a sub-tree pointer is zero, the code jumps past the entire subtree instead of visiting each empty block. The traversals are also capped by the file's logical/compressed size via `total_logical_blocks`, eliminating millions of unnecessary empty-block checks on huge files.

## Invariant: collision-free, monotone allocation

Two consecutive allocations never return the same block: `allocate_with_hint` sets a bit immediately after finding it, and the hint advances past it, so the next allocation starts strictly ahead. This is a Kani-verified property (`src/allocator.rs`) and is what makes the sequential hint path safe under concurrent access serialized by the `DiskManager` mutex.

## Extension seams

Allocation is centralized behind the `BlockAllocator` trait (`src/allocator.rs`), so alternative allocation strategies could be added without touching the write path. The hint machinery, bitmap word scanning, the indirect addressing tree, `AllocSim`, and the contiguous-run allocator are independent seams — each was optimized without altering the others.

nodes.title: Compression and Pre-compression Filters
nodes.description: How OIFS combines zstd compression (with multi-frame EOF append, seekable 64K chunked compression with COW extent swap, and read-modify-recompress fallback) with Blosc2-style pre-compression filters (Delta, ByteShuffle, BitShuffle, TruncPrecision). Covers the Zstd thread-local pool, persistent scoped worker pool, DecodedBlobCache (4 slots, 16 MiB/entry, 32 MiB cap) for non-seekable reads, ChunkReadCache (8 slots) for seekable reads, and cache invalidation across write, truncate, delete, migrate, defrag, and reload.
nodes.body:
## Responsibility and ownership

The write, read, and filter pipeline live across several modules. `write_data_with_filters` (`src/disk.rs#L4432-L4728`) orchestrates the full staging sequence — pre-compression filter → zstd compression → encryption — while `filters.rs` (`src/filters.rs`) provides the filter primitives, the config stored on the inode, the native C-Blosc2 wrapper, and entropy analysis. `disk/chunked.rs` implements the seekable 64KB chunked fast path (random reads/writes, COW extent swap). `disk/caches.rs` provides `DecodedBlobCache` (whole-file decoded blob cache for non-seekable compressed/encrypted files) and `ChunkReadCache` (per-chunk decompression cache for seekable files). `zstd_pool.rs` manages thread-local Zstd contexts and a persistent scoped worker pool used for parallel chunk compression/decompression.

## The write-stage pipeline

Every initial write (`file_offset == 0`) flows through `plan_write_prepared` (`src/disk.rs#L881-L1057`), which applies a fixed, ordered staging pipeline. The reverse order is used on read (decrypt → decompress → unapply filter).

1. **Pre-compression filter** — `apply_filters_cow` transforms the raw payload into a more compressible form. This runs *before* compression so filters can collapse Shannon entropy that a generic LZ77 compressor cannot reuse.
2. **Compression** — governed by `CompressionMode` (`src/disk.rs#L66-L78`):
   - `Always`: always zstd (level 0).
   - `Never`: never compress.
   - `Auto` (default): compress only when the filtered data is ≥ 8KB, and only keep the compressed result if it is actually smaller than the working data.
   - `Stream { level }`: full-file stream compression with explicit Zstd level.
   - `Seekable { chunk_size, level }`: fixed 64KB chunked compression with O(1) random access.
3. **Encryption** — if a key is present, the (already compressed) data is encrypted with XChaCha20-Poly1305 and a fresh per-file nonce. Compressing before encrypting preserves compression ratio while keeping ciphertext entropy flat.

The ordering filter→compress→encrypt is why both `inode.compressed_size` (physical) and `inode.size` (logical) are tracked separately, and why the filter flags (`filter_typesize`, `filter_delta`, `filter_shuffle`, `filter_bitshuffle`) must be recorded on the inode to reverse the pipeline on read.

## Zero-copy filter staging

`apply_filters_cow` (`src/filters.rs#L829-L835`) returns a `Cow<[u8]>`: `Cow::Borrowed(data)` (zero allocation) when the filter is inactive or the typesize is not one of {1, 2, 4, 8}, and `Cow::Owned` only when a pipeline actually runs. On the common unfiltered/unencrypted path this eliminates every intermediate buffer copy — reported as up to ~28,500x speedup on 1MB payloads — and lets the uncompressed bytes flow straight into the write.

## Zstd thread-local pool and persistent scoped worker pool

`zstd_pool.rs` eliminates per-call `CCtx`/`DCtx` allocation overhead through two layers:

1. **Thread-local pools** — each thread keeps one compressor per compression level and one decompressor in `thread_local!` storage. On drop, contexts are returned to a global `Mutex`-protected pool (`MAX_GLOBAL_COMPRESSORS_PER_LEVEL = 32`, `MAX_GLOBAL_DECOMPRESSORS = 32`) for reuse by other threads.
2. **Persistent scoped worker pool** — `par_for_index(total, f)` spawns `num_cpus - 1` worker threads (clamped to 1..15) named `oifs-chunk-w{N}` at first use. Workers park on a `Condvar`; each dispatch increments a generation counter, avoiding `pthread_create` churn and keeping thread-local Zstd contexts warm across calls. The calling thread participates via dynamic work-stealing (`next.fetch_add`), falling back to sequential execution when `total <= 1` or another dispatch already holds the pool lock.

`compress_frame` and `decompress_frame_into` are the primary hot-path entry points used by both the stream append path and the chunked pipeline.

## Compression modes and append behavior

`write_data_with_filters` handles non-offset-0 writes with three distinct strategies for already-compressed files:

- **Seekable 64K Chunked Compression (P4.2 fast path)** — When `INODE_FLAG_SEEKABLE_64K` is active or `CompressionMode::Seekable` is selected, writes enter the 3-stage out-of-lock pipeline (`write_chunked_64k_pipeline`, `src/disk/chunked.rs#L1702-L1860`). Only affected 64KB chunks are re-encoded and swapped via COW extents, eliminating full-file rewrites.
- **Zstd Multi-Frame Append (stream fast path)** — When appending strictly at EOF (`file_offset == inode.size`) to an *unencrypted* stream-compressed file with *no* active filters, the new chunk is compressed as an independent Zstd frame via `zstd_pool::compress_frame` and appended at `compressed_size`. Because `zstd::stream::decode_all` transparently decodes concatenated frames, no existing block is decompressed or rewritten.
- **Read-Modify-Recompress (stream fallback)** — For encrypted stream files, random-offset stream writes, or files with active filters, the full payload is decompressed, the change is spliced in, old blocks are freed, and the file is rewritten contiguously from offset 0 with an effective filter config that recovers the inode's stored filter flags.

Raw (uncompressed) files use a plain in-place `write_buffer_at_offset` write that does not participate in the frame pipeline.

## Seekable 64KB Chunked Compression (P4.2)

To avoid $O(N)$ full-payload decompression on random reads and partial writes, OIFS implements **Seekable 64KB Chunked Compression**:

- **Fixed 64KB Logical Chunks**: Files are partitioned into uniform 64KB chunks (`CHUNK_SIZE_64K = 65536`).
- **64-bit ChunkEntry**: Stored directly in the inode block table, each 8-byte entry packs `start_block: u32`, `block_count: u8`, `flags: u8` (`FLAG_RAW` or `FLAG_COMPRESSED`), and `compressed_len: u16` (`src/inode.rs#L89-L119`).
- **Copy-on-Write (COW) Extent Swap**: Updating data at any offset (`write_chunked_64k_internal`, `src/disk/chunked.rs#L1702-L1860`) allocates new physical contiguous blocks, writes compressed or raw bytes, atomically updates the chunk pointer (`set_logical_chunk_entry`), and then frees the old blocks.
- **Anti-Inflation Fallback**: If a compressed chunk does not strictly save space (or exceeds 64KB), it is stored as uncompressed `FLAG_RAW` blocks, eliminating negative compression overhead.
- **$O(1)$ Random Reads**: `read_at_chunked_64k` (`src/disk/chunked.rs#L591-L780`) decodes only the single targeted 64KB chunk directly into the caller's buffer without decompressing the entire file, completely bypassing stateful file offset tracking.
- **Sequential Read-Ahead**: For sequential sub-chunk reads, the read path detects the pattern (current chunk miss + previous chunk hit in cache) and prefetches up to 4 subsequent chunks in parallel via `par_for_index`, inserting them into `ChunkReadCache` under a single write lock acquisition.

### Mermaid diagram: Seekable Chunked Layout

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph Inode["Inode Block Table"]
        D0["blocks[0]"]
        D1["blocks[1]"]
        D2["blocks[2]"]
        D9["blocks[9]"]
        SIB["blocks[10] (Single Indirect)"]
        DIB["blocks[11] (Double Indirect)"]
        TIB["triple_indirect"]
    end

    subgraph ChunkEntries["ChunkEntry Array (packed in leaf slots)"]
        CE0["ChunkEntry[0]: start_blk=100, count=16, flags=COMPRESSED, len=45056"]
        CE1["ChunkEntry[1]: start_blk=116, count=8, flags=RAW, len=32768"]
        CE2["ChunkEntry[2]: EMPTY (sparse hole)"]
    end

    subgraph DataBlocks["Physical Data Blocks (4 KiB each)"]
        B100["Block 100"]
        B101["Block 101"]
        B115["Block 115"]
        B116["Block 116"]
        B123["Block 123"]
    end

    D0 --> CE0
    D1 --> CE1
    D2 --> CE2
    CE0 -->|"16 contiguous blocks"| B100
    CE0 --> B115
    CE1 -->|"8 contiguous blocks"| B116
    CE1 --> B123
    CE2 -.->|"no blocks allocated"| B100
```

Each logical chunk index maps through the inode's pointer tree (direct → single indirect → double indirect → triple indirect) to a leaf slot holding a `ChunkEntry`. The entry's `start_block` and `block_count` describe a **contiguous run** of physical blocks storing that chunk's compressed or raw payload.

## Read acceleration caches

### DecodedBlobCache (non-seekable files)

`DecodedBlobCache` (`src/disk/caches.rs#L92-L163`) is a bounded LRU cache for whole-file decoded payloads of **stream-compressed or whole-file encrypted** files. It eliminates the $O(\text{calls} \times \text{file\_size})$ full-file decode cliff when callers issue sequential or random sub-file `read_at` calls on non-seekable blobs.

- **Capacity**: 4 entries (`MAX_ENTRIES = 4`)
- **Per-entry limit**: 16 MiB (`MAX_ENTRY_BYTES = 16 * 1024 * 1024`)
- **Total cap**: 32 MiB (`MAX_TOTAL_BYTES = 32 * 1024 * 1024`)
- **Key**: `(inode_id, size, compressed_size, first_block, nonce)` — any metadata change invalidates the entry.
- **Lookup**: Under shared read lock in `read_at_with_inode` (`src/disk.rs#L3765-L3785`). If present, slices directly from the `Arc<Vec<u8>>` into the caller's buffer. If absent and file ≤ 16 MiB, decodes the full payload, inserts into cache, then slices.
- **Eviction**: LRU by insertion order; evicts from front when either entry count or total bytes would exceed limits.

### ChunkReadCache (seekable files)

`ChunkReadCache` (`src/disk/caches.rs#L1-L75`) is an 8-slot LRU cache for **individual 64KB chunk** decompressions of seekable chunked files.

- **Capacity**: 8 entries (`CAPACITY = 8`)
- **Key**: `(inode_id, chunk_idx, raw_entry, valid_len)` — any chunk rewrite (new `raw_entry`) invalidates the cached version.
- **Lookup**: `copy_slice_if_hit` copies the requested sub-range directly from the cached `Arc<[u8]>` into the caller's buffer under the shared read lock, avoiding `Arc` clone/drop atomic traffic on hits.
- **Prefetch**: Sequential access detection triggers parallel prefetch of up to 4 subsequent chunks via `par_for_index`, inserting all into the cache under a single write lock.

### Cache invalidation

`invalidate_payload_caches(inode_id)` (`src/disk.rs#L656-L664`) clears **both** caches for a given inode. It is invoked on:

| Operation | Location |
|-----------|----------|
| **Write** (any `write_data_with_filters` path, including chunked) | `src/disk.rs#L4856`, `src/disk/chunked.rs#L1538`, `src/disk/chunked.rs#L1899` |
| **Truncate** (`truncate`, `truncate_chunked_64k`) | `src/disk.rs#L5841`, `src/disk/chunked.rs#L1665` |
| **Delete** (journal replay of `SetInodeBitmap { allocated: false }`) | `src/disk.rs#L2241` |
| **Migrate** (inode format v1→v2 rewrite) | `src/disk/maintenance.rs#L119` (`guard.clear_payload_caches()`) |
| **Defragment** (safe mode live-reload, in-place defrag) | `src/disk/maintenance.rs#L293` (`guard.clear_payload_caches()`) |
| **Reload** (after safe defrag atomic swap) | `src/disk/maintenance.rs#L293` (`guard.clear_payload_caches()`) |

`clear_payload_caches()` wipes both caches entirely; `invalidate_inode(inode_id)` is the targeted version.

## Blosc2-style pre-compression filters

`filters.rs` ships four composable filters (`FilterType`), each lossless except TruncPrecision:

- **Delta** — first-order difference of typed elements (`delta_encode_inplace`), collapsing linear/temporal sequences into small integers.
- **ByteShuffle** — transposes Array-of-Structures to Structure-of-Arrays, clustering high-order bytes (`shuffle_encode`).
- **BitShuffle** — 8×8 bit-matrix transposition per 64-bit word using the symmetric Delta-Swap `transpose_8x8_u64` primitive, effective for sparse/bitfield data.
- **TruncPrecision** — zeroes least-significant mantissa bits of f32/f64 (`trunc_precision_encode_inplace`); it is lossy, so its inverse is identity.

These are orchestrated by `FilterPipeline` (`src/filters.rs#L19-L70`), whose `apply` runs filters in order and `unapply` runs them in reverse. The compact `FilterConfig` (`src/filters.rs#L99-L186`) stored on the inode exposes factory helpers (`numeric`, `delta_only`, `shuffle_only`, `bitshuffle_only`, `custom`) and `to_pipeline`. Native C-Blosc2 integration is available via `blosc2_compress` / `blosc2_decompress` (`src/filters.rs#L73-L95`), which build `CParams` and use the compiled C-Blosc2 chunk codec.

### FilterConfig persistence

`FilterConfig` is serialized into the Inode as four dedicated fields (`src/inode.rs#L33-L65`):

```rust
pub filter_typesize: u8,    // element size (1,2,4,8) — 0 = no filters
pub filter_delta: bool,     // Delta filter enabled
pub filter_shuffle: bool,   // ByteShuffle filter enabled
pub filter_bitshuffle: bool // BitShuffle filter enabled
```

This avoids any per-inode heap allocation and makes the filter config trivially copyable with the inode.

### Pipeline ordering

`FilterPipeline::apply` runs filters in declaration order (Delta → ByteShuffle → BitShuffle → TruncPrecision), while `unapply` runs their inverses in reverse. The `FilterConfig::to_pipeline` builder respects the same order: Delta first, then ByteShuffle, then BitShuffle.

## Entropy analysis and recommendation

`calculate_entropy` (`src/filters.rs#L668-L685`) computes Shannon entropy in bits/byte. `recommend_filters` (`src/filters.rs#L910-L1077`) evaluates 14 candidate pipelines:

- Raw (no filter)
- Delta at typesizes 1, 2, 4, 8
- ByteShuffle at typesizes 2, 4, 8
- BitShuffle at typesizes 2, 4, 8
- Delta+ByteShuffle ("numeric") at typesizes 2, 4, 8

For inputs > 256 KB, it samples three 64 KB windows (head, middle, tail, each 8-byte aligned) and scales results. Evaluation runs in parallel across CPU cores via `std::thread::scope` (not Rayon). The configuration with the smallest projected zstd size wins. This backs the `filter-analyze` CLI and `put --filter auto`. The whole filter family is covered by Kani bijectivity proofs (`src/filters.rs#L1114+`), including the unaligned-tail case and composite pipelines.

## Extension seams

Filters are layered on compression rather than fused into it: any new filter is a new `FilterType` plus matching (un)apply functions, and the pipeline applies and reverses them generically. `FilterConfig` is the single seam between the filter layer and the inode, so new filters require no changes to the write or read paths beyond adding the boolean/byte fields only if the compact config needs more independent settings.

nodes.title: Concurrency & Session Model
nodes.description: The OifsSession abstraction with three modes — Standalone (direct mmap, zero IPC), Local (Unix Domain Sockets in per-user private directory), Network (TCP + rendezvous file with clock-free active Ping/Pong) — master election via bind_or_connect, transparent failover, session registry with canonical path dedup, poison-recovered locks for registries/caches, and length-prefixed Bincode IPC frame protocol with challenge-response authentication.
nodes.body:
## Responsibility and ownership

The session layer owns the process coordination contract while the IPC layer owns the transport. `OifsSession` (`src/session.rs#L60-L79`) decides whether a given process runs in **Direct (Master)** or **Remote (Proxy)** mode and forwards every operation to the right place. `src/ipc.rs` provides the `bind_or_connect` master election, the `IpcServer` request dispatcher, and the length-prefixed framing used on every hop. The actual mutation of the image happens inside a single Master's `DiskManager` (`Arc<RwLock<DiskManagerInner>>`), which provides shared parallel reader access and exclusive writer serialization with a dedicated `sync_mutex` for physical durability flushes.

## Session mode taxonomy

OIFS supports three **SessionMode** variants (`src/ipc.rs#L39-L52`):

| Mode | Transport | IPC Overhead | Use Case |
|------|-----------|--------------|----------|
| `Standalone` (default) | None — direct `mmap` | Zero sockets, zero background threads | Single-process, CLI, embedded, testing |
| `Local` | Unix Domain Socket in per-user private runtime directory (`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/oifs` or `/tmp/oifs-<uid>/oifs`) | One background `IpcServer` thread on the Master; clients forward over UDS | Multi-process on one machine, containers, CI |
| `Network` | TCP + rendezvous `.image.master` file in image directory + **clock-free active Ping/Pong** probe | Master binds TCP; clients connect over TCP | NFS/Lustre, multi-node clusters, remote mounts |

**Standalone** is not a third variant of `OifsSession` — it is simply `SessionMode::Standalone` which produces a `Direct` session **without** starting an `IpcServer`. The `OifsSession` enum itself has only two variants (`src/session.rs#L60-L79`):

```rust
pub enum OifsSession {
    Direct { dm: Arc<DiskManager>, server: Option<Arc<IpcServer>>, ... },
    Remote { client: Arc<IpcClient>, dm_fallback: Arc<Mutex<Option<Arc<DiskManager>>>>, ... },
}
```

- **Direct**: owns the `DiskManager` (and optionally a background `IpcServer`). Used by Master in Local/Network modes, and by **all** processes in Standalone mode.
- **Remote**: holds an `IpcClient` connection pool to the Master, plus a `dm_fallback` slot used during transparent failover.

## Master election: `bind_or_connect`

Master election is transport-specific and implemented in `bind_or_connect` (`src/ipc.rs#L887-L1010`). The function either binds as Master (returning `MasterOrClient::Master`) or connects as Client (returning `MasterOrClient::Client`).

### Local mode (UDS)

1. Deterministic socket path: `get_socket_path` (`src/ipc.rs#L123-L144`) derives `<private_runtime_dir>/oifs_<name>_<hash>.sock` from the canonical image path. The parent directory is created mode `0700`; the socket itself is created mode `0600`. A companion `.tok` file holds the session secret, also `0600`.
2. Process first **tries to connect** to the existing socket (up to 10 attempts, 15 ms apart).
3. If connection fails, it **removes any stale socket/token** and attempts to `bind`.
4. If `bind` fails with `EADDRINUSE`, it retries connecting (up to 15 attempts), then removes the stale socket and retries `bind` once more.
5. On success as Master: generates a fresh 32-byte session secret (`auth_secret`), writes it atomically to the `.tok` file, and starts the `IpcServer`.

### Network mode (TCP + rendezvous file)

1. Rendezvous file path: `get_master_info_path` (`src/ipc.rs#L146-L158`) returns `<image_dir>/.<image_name>.master`.
2. If the file exists, reads `MasterInfo { addr, pid, auth_token }` and runs **clock-free active Ping/Pong probe** (`is_tcp_master_alive`, `src/ipc.rs#L159-L179`): connects to `addr`, sends `IpcRequest::Ping`, expects `Pong` within 500 ms. If probe succeeds, connects as Client.
3. If probe fails or file missing: attempts **atomic `create_new`** on the rendezvous file. Winner becomes Master:
   - Binds TCP listener on `bind_addr` (default `127.0.0.1:0` — loopback only; non-loopback requires explicit opt-in `is_loopback_bind`, `src/ipc.rs#L160-L180`).
   - Generates `auth_secret`, writes `MasterInfo` with hex-encoded token to rendezvous file (mode `0600`).
   - Starts `IpcServer` on the TCP listener.
4. Losers read the rendezvous file, connect to the published `addr`, and authenticate with the published `auth_token`.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant P1 as Process 1
    participant P2 as Process 2
    participant FS as Filesystem (rendezvous / socket)

    Note over P1,P2: Local Mode (UDS)
    P1->>FS: connect(socket) --> fails
    P1->>FS: bind(socket) --> succeeds
    P1->>FS: write .tok (auth_secret)
    P1->>P1: start IpcServer

    P2->>FS: connect(socket) --> succeeds
    P2->>FS: read .tok --> auth_secret
    P2->>P1: AuthChallenge/Response over UDS
    P1->>P2: AuthVerify (mutual proof)

    Note over P1,P2: Network Mode (TCP)
    P1->>FS: create_new(.master) --> succeeds
    P1->>FS: write MasterInfo{addr, pid, auth_token}
    P1->>P1: bind TCP, start IpcServer

    P2->>FS: read .master --> MasterInfo
    P2->>P1: TCP connect(addr)
    P2->>P1: Ping (active probe)
    P1->>P2: Pong
    P2->>P1: AuthChallenge/Response over TCP
    P1->>P2: AuthVerify
```

## Process-wide session registry

`SESSION_REGISTRY` (`src/session.rs#L77-L81`) is a process-wide `OnceLock<Mutex<HashMap<PathBuf, OifsSession>>>` keyed by the **canonicalized absolute path**. `canonicalize_path` (`src/session.rs#L84-L131`) resolves symlinks (up to 32 hops) so all links pointing at the same image deduplicate to the same registry key.

`get_or_open_with_mode` (`src/session.rs#L195-L215`):
1. Acquires `lock_unpoisoned` on the registry mutex.
2. If a session exists for the canonical key, returns a `Clone` (which clones the inner `Arc` fields — threads share one Master with natural reference counting).
3. Otherwise, constructs a new session via `open_with_mode_retry`, inserts it, and returns the clone.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[Thread calls get_or_open_with_mode] --> B[canonicalize_path resolves symlinks]
    B --> C{Registry has key?}
    C -- Yes --> D[Return Arc-clone of existing OifsSession]
    C -- No --> E[open_with_mode_retry]
    E --> F{bind_or_connect}
    F -- Master --> G[Create DiskManager, start IpcServer, Direct session]
    F -- Client --> H[Connect, authenticate, Remote session]
    G --> I[Insert into registry]
    H --> I
    I --> J[Return session]
```

## IPC frame protocol

Every RPC is a **length-prefixed Bincode frame** (`src/ipc.rs#L306-L335`) with a **128 MiB hard cap** (`MAX_FRAME_BYTES`). Frames larger than this are rejected **before any allocation**.

- **Encoding**: `bincode::DefaultOptions` with fixint encoding, trailing bytes allowed, and a per-frame byte limit (`frame_codec`, `src/ipc.rs#L331-L339`).
- **Thread-local pooled buffers**: Separate read/write buffers (`FRAME_READ_BUF`, `FRAME_WRITE_BUF`) reused across frames; large buffers are shrunk after use (`shrink_frame_buf`, `src/ipc.rs#L354-L358`).
- **Streaming read**: Payload streamed in 64 KiB chunks into the pooled buffer (`FRAME_READ_CHUNK`), never allocating the announced size up front (`read_framed`, `src/ipc.rs#L370-L403`).
- **Single dispatcher**: `IpcServer::handle_request` (`src/ipc.rs#L699-L780`) maps each `IpcRequest` variant to a `DiskManager` call. Logic is **never duplicated** across Direct and Remote arms.

## IPC authentication: challenge-response with mutual proof

Authentication is mandatory for all data operations. Ping is allowed unauthenticated for the active probe.

### Credential types (`src/ipc.rs#L432-L440`)

```rust
pub enum AuthCredential {
    Password(String),      // Filesystem password (encrypted images)
    Secret([u8; 32]),      // Session secret published by Master (plain images)
}
```

### Handshake flow

1. **Client → Master**: `AuthChallenge { client_nonce[32], has_password: bool }`
   - Client sends a fresh random nonce. **Password never travels in cleartext**.
2. **Master → Client**: `AuthChallenge { server_nonce[32], salt[16], encrypted: bool }`
   - Master replies with its nonce, the image's encryption salt, and whether the image is encrypted.
   - If encrypted and client sent `has_password=false`, Master immediately rejects with "Password required".
3. **Client computes MAC**: `client_mac = BLAKE2b-MAC(key, transcript(0, client_nonce, server_nonce, salt))`
   - Key = Argon2id(password, salt) for encrypted images; key = session secret for plain images.
4. **Client → Master**: `AuthResponse { client_mac[32] }`
5. **Master verifies client_mac**, then computes `server_mac = BLAKE2b-MAC(key, transcript(1, ...))` and returns `AuthVerify { server_mac }`.
6. **Client verifies server_mac** — proves Master holds the same key, detecting redirection to a fake Master.

**Domain separation**: transcript includes constant `AUTH_DOMAIN = b"oifs-ipc-auth-v1"`. Direction byte (0/1) prevents tag interchangeability. Constant-time comparison (`ct_eq`) for MACs.

### Where the key comes from

- **Encrypted image**: `DiskManager` derives Argon2id key from password + salt at open time. `auth_key()` returns the 32-byte IPC auth key. Master uses this for all peers.
- **Plain image**: Master generates random 32-byte `auth_secret` at startup, publishes it in `.tok` (Local) or `.master` (Network). Clients read it and use as `AuthCredential::Secret`.

### Security properties

- Password never on wire (even encrypted).
- Mutual authentication — client verifies Master.
- Session secret is owner-readable only (`0600`).
- Per-connection 10 s handshake timeout (`AUTH_HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT`) prevents Slowloris.
- Max 256 concurrent unauthenticated peers (`MAX_CONCURRENT_PEERS`) bounds resource exhaustion.

## IpcServer architecture

- **Listener thread** (`src/ipc.rs#L1070-L1140`): non-blocking listener fd, `libc::poll` with 50 ms timeout, accepts connections, spawns **one dedicated worker thread per peer**.
- **Worker thread** (`src/ipc.rs#L1142-L1300`): per-connection authentication state machine; after auth, loops reading framed requests, dispatches to `handle_request`, writes framed response. Emits `SessionEvent::PeerConnected`, `RequestHandled`, `PeerDisconnected` via bounded channel (`MAX_PENDING_SESSION_EVENTS = 1024`).
- **Drop**: graceful shutdown — waits up to 1.5 s for active peers, then removes socket/rendezvous file.

## IpcClient connection pool

- **Bounded pool**: up to `MAX_CLIENT_POOL_STREAMS = 8` concurrent authenticated streams (`src/ipc.rs#L1407-L1412`).
- **Checkout protocol**: `CheckedOutStream` RAII guard ensures a stream is either in the pool **or** checked out for one RPC. On panic or I/O error mid-exchange, `Drop` closes the desynchronized socket and decrements `total_streams` — never returns a potentially desynchronized socket to the pool.
- **Lazy secondary streams**: Single-threaded callers use one socket; concurrent callers open additional streams on demand, each re-authenticating using the cached `ClientAuthCache` (Argon2id key or session secret, zeroized on drop).

## Transparent failover (self-healing)

A Remote session survives Master loss (crash, power loss, network partition) without caller intervention. Implemented in `send_request` (`src/session.rs#L768-L848`):

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Client as Remote Session
    participant Master as Master Process
    participant FS as Filesystem

    Client->>Master: RPC over UDS/TCP
    Master--xClient: Connection error (broken pipe, reset, EOF)
    Note over Client: is_connection_error() matches
    loop Up to 5 attempts
        Client->>FS: Re-run bind_or_connect (master election)
        alt Becomes new Master
            Client->>Client: Create local DiskManager
            Client->>Client: Pin as dm_fallback (lock_unpoisoned)
            Client->>Client: Set has_fallback = true
            Client->>Client: Serve RPC locally via handle_request
        else Connects to new Master
            Client->>Client: Update IpcClient to new connection
            Client->>Master: Retry RPC on new connection
        end
    end
```

- **Lock-free fast path**: `has_fallback: AtomicBool` checked before acquiring `dm_fallback` mutex (`src/session.rs#L773-L779`).
- **Fallback promotion**: When a Remote process wins election, it pins a local `DiskManager` as `dm_fallback` and continues serving locally — the session **becomes Direct** transparently.
- **Password persistence**: Remote session stores the password in a `Zeroizing<String>` for automatic reconnection (`src/session.rs#L75-L76`, `#L664`).

## Reader parallelism and lock hierarchy

Within the Master process, concurrency is managed by a fine-grained hierarchy (`src/disk.rs`):

1. **Shared Read Lock** (`inner.read()`): Multiple reader threads calling `read_at` or `read_data` acquire a shared `RwLock` read guard concurrently, executing zero-copy memory reads with no reader-reader contention.
2. **Dedicated Flush Mutex** (`sync_mutex: Arc<Mutex<()>>`): Physical disk flushes via `flush_range` / `msync` acquire `sync_mutex` **without holding the inner write lock** (`src/disk.rs#L1560`, `#L5397`, `#L5468`), ensuring durable background writebacks never stall concurrent readers.
3. **Exclusive Write Lock** (`inner.write()`): Allocation, bitmap updates, and inode commits acquire an exclusive lock during the commit phase, ensuring full mutual exclusion.

The `DiskManager` struct holds:
```rust
inner: Arc<RwLock<DiskManagerInner>>,   // guards all on-disk metadata
sync_mutex: Arc<Mutex<()>>,              // serializes msync only
```

## Poison-recovered locks: `lock_unpoisoned` / `read_unpoisoned` / `write_unpoisoned`

Some mutexes guard **reconstructible in-memory state** (registries, caches, coordination flags) where a panic mid-critical-section cannot leave the data inconsistent. For these, propagating poison would permanently brick the subsystem — one unrelated panic anywhere would make every later acquisition fail.

**Helpers in `src/lib.rs#L42-L68`**:

```rust
pub(crate) fn lock_unpoisoned<T>(m: &Mutex<T>) -> MutexGuard<'_, T> {
    m.lock().unwrap_or_else(PoisonError::into_inner)
}
pub(crate) fn read_unpoisoned<T>(r: &RwLock<T>) -> RwLockReadGuard<'_, T> {
    r.read().unwrap_or_else(PoisonError::into_inner)
}
pub(crate) fn write_unpoisoned<T>(r: &RwLock<T>) -> RwLockWriteGuard<'_, T> {
    r.write().unwrap_or_else(PoisonError::into_inner)
}
```

**Where used** (recover from poison):

- `SESSION_REGISTRY` mutex (`src/session.rs#L285`, `#L304`, `#L311`)
- `IpcClient` connection pool mutex (`src/ipc.rs#L1443`, `#L1454`, `#L1480`, `#L1618`, `#L1646`, `#L1758`)
- Auto-defrag config/stats/worker mutexes (`src/auto_defrag.rs#L187-L215`)
- Async flush pending ranges (`src/disk.rs#L555`, `#L580`, `#L1563`, `#L5428`, `#L5471`)
- Decoded blob cache (`src/disk.rs#L3756`, `#L3761`, `#L4840`, `#L4845`, `#L9088`, `#L9221`)
- FUSE handle map, parent map (`src/fuse.rs#L2242-L2272`, `#L2665-L#2670`)
- Sharded directory cache: `read_shard`/`write_shard`/`for_each_mut` (`src/disk/caches.rs#L233`, `#L241`, `#L251`, `#L257`)

**Where NOT used** (poison propagates, as required for on-disk consistency):
- `DiskManagerInner` RwLock — guards bitmap, inode tables, block allocation. A panic here could leave on-disk structures inconsistent; the process must fail fast.
- Inode cache shards use `.unwrap()` directly (`src/disk/caches.rs#L398`, `#L403`, `#L408`, `#L416`, `#L422`)

## 32-shard lock striping for caches

Both the inode cache and directory cache use **32 shards** with **Fibonacci hashing** (`0x517cc1b727220a95`) for uniform distribution, eliminating lock contention across concurrent accesses to different inodes/directories.

### BoundedInodeCache (`src/disk/caches.rs#L354-L423`)

- **32 shards** (`NUM_INODE_CACHE_SHARDS`), each with independent `RwLock<InodeCacheShard>`.
- **Second-Chance (Clock) eviction**: each entry has an atomic `referenced` bit. On cache hit under shared lock, bit is set (`Relaxed`). Eviction walks the queue, gives referenced entries a second chance (clears bit, re-queues), evicts unreferenced.
- **Fibonacci shard index**: `(inode_id * 0x517cc1b727220a95) & 31` — consecutive inode IDs never map to the same shard.
- **Capacity**: `INODE_CACHE_CAPACITY = 2048` total, ~64 per shard.
- **Single-entry eviction**: Reaching capacity evicts only one entry (old behavior wiped entire cache).

### ShardedDirCache (`src/disk/caches.rs#L201-L260`)

- **32 shards** (`NUM_DIR_CACHE_SHARDS`), each `RwLock<FxHashMap<u64, DirIndex>>`.
- **Same Fibonacci hashing**: `(dir_inode_id * 0x517cc1b727220a95) & 31`.
- **DirIndex** caches positive lookups; promotes to `complete` after `DIR_INDEX_BUILD_AFTER_SCANS = 8` cold scans or a negative lookup.
- On encrypted filesystems, maintains both `stored` (ciphertext names) and `plain` (plaintext names) maps to skip re-encryption.
- **Lock striping** ensures `create_file`/`delete_file` on one directory never stalls `lookup`/`resolve_path`/`list_dir` on another.

### FxHasher (`src/lib.rs#L101-L164`)

```rust
const K: usize = 0x517cc1b727220a95usize;
```
Fast non-cryptographic hash for integer keys; processes 8/4/2/1 bytes at a time with rotate-xor-multiply.

## Out-of-lock pipeline: filter → compress → encrypt

Write operations split into three stages so CPU-bound work happens **without holding filesystem locks** (`src/disk.rs#L5671-L5850`):

### Stage 1 — Shared Read Lock (inspection)
- Acquires `inner.read()`.
- Determines write case (FullOverwrite / CompressedAppend / Recompress / Raw).
- Reads existing decompressed content if needed for splice/recompress.
- **Drops read lock immediately** after collecting all metadata.

### Stage 2 — Zero Locks (CPU-bound processing)
- **Filter**: `apply_filters_cow` / `unapply_filters_in_place` (Delta, Shuffle, Bitshuffle).
- **Compress**: Zstd multi-frame via pooled `CCtx` (seekable 64K) or single frame (stream).
- **Encrypt**: XChaCha20-Poly1305 with per-file AAD (inode_id + scheme) — stack-staged, zero allocation.
- Produces a `WritePlan` with final bytes, new sizes, encryption nonce, physical offset.

### Stage 3 — Exclusive Write Lock (commit)
- Acquires `inner.write()`.
- Verifies inode unchanged since Stage 1 (re-plans if raced).
- Allocates/frees blocks, writes payload at `phys_off`.
- Updates inode metadata (size, compressed_size, nonce, filter flags).
- Flushes via `sync_mutex` (range-based or full) **after dropping write lock**.

This three-stage design means:
- Concurrent readers never block on compression/encryption CPU.
- Only the short metadata commit phase holds the exclusive lock.
- `sync_mutex` serializes `msync` without blocking readers.

## Zero-allocation path resolution: `resolve_path_iter` + `resolve_parent`

Path resolution avoids heap allocation by iterating over `&str` slices directly (`src/disk.rs#L6437-L6620`):

```rust
fn resolve_path_iter<'a>(
    guard: &DiskManagerInner,
    parts: impl Iterator<Item = &'a str>,
) -> Result<u64, DiskManagerError> {
    let mut curr = guard.superblock.root_inode;
    for part in parts {
        // validation, '..' rejection
        curr = Self::dir_lookup(guard, curr, part)? ...
    }
    Ok(curr)
}

pub fn resolve_path(&self, path: &str) -> Result<u64, DiskManagerError> {
    let guard = self.inner.read().unwrap();
    Self::resolve_path_iter(
        &guard,
        path.split('/').filter(|s| !s.is_empty() && *s != "."),
    )
}

pub fn resolve_parent(&self, path: &str) -> Result<(u64, String), DiskManagerError> {
    // splits once via rsplit_once('/'), then delegates to resolve_path_iter
}
```

- **No allocation**: `split('/')` yields `&str` views into the original string.
- **Single read lock**: entire resolution holds one `inner.read()` guard.
- **~11.9M lookups/sec** on typical hardware (benchmark: `cargo bench resolve_path`).
- `resolve_parent` reuses the same iterator for the parent portion, returning the final component as an owned `String` only for the filename.

## POSIX OpenMode and race safety

`DiskManager::open_file` and `OifsSession::open_file` provide POSIX-standard file creation semantics (`src/session.rs#L870-L888`):

| OpenMode | Behavior |
|----------|----------|
| `OpenExisting` | Returns existing inode ID or `ENOENT` |
| `CreateNew` | Atomically creates file or returns `EEXIST` (`AlreadyExists`) |
| `CreateOrOpen` | Opens if present, creates if missing |

Under concurrent execution, `create_file` uses **double-checked locking** within directory blocks: even under aggressive multi-threaded races on non-existent files, exactly one thread succeeds while contenders receive `EEXIST`, preventing duplicate directory entries or orphan inodes.

## Block-level merge policy and Copy-on-Write (COW)

All mutations funnel through the **single Master's `DiskManagerInner` mutex** (exclusive write lock). The merge rules are:

- **Disjoint byte offsets in the same block** merge in place — each write modifies only its own byte range.
- **Overlapping offsets** are **Last-Writer-Wins** because the exclusive lock serializes writes into POSIX `pwrite` semantics with no torn writes.
- **Seekable 64K Chunked Compression** uses COW: updating data inside a chunk allocates fresh physical blocks, writes the payload, atomically swaps the inode `ChunkEntry` pointer, and frees the previous blocks. Readers never observe partially updated blocks.
- **Stream compressed files** use zstd multi-frame append at EOF, or transparent read-modify-recompress for random offsets.

This single-writer model (enforced by the Master-Proxy architecture) is the **sole source of write serialization** — there are no per-block locks or finer-grained coordination.

nodes.title: Online Defragmentation
nodes.description: How OIFS analyzes filesystem fragmentation using 64-bit bitmap scanning and performs both safe (out-of-place rebuild with atomic rename) and WAL-atomic in-place defragmentation, including ChunkEntry relocation for seekable files, shift_table_collapse for chunk table compaction, and a background auto-defrag coordinator.
nodes.body:
## Responsibility and ownership

Defragmentation and space reorganization logic reside entirely within [`DiskManager`](repo://src/disk.rs). It evaluates disk layout health through [`analyze_fragmentation`](repo://src/disk/maintenance.rs#L137-L166), which measures free-block scattering across physical data space. Defragmentation execution is exposed via [`DiskManager::defragment`](repo://src/disk/maintenance.rs#L460-L480), supporting two operational modes:

- `DefragMode::Safe` (default): An out-of-place reorganization in a temporary image followed by transactional verification and a 3-step atomic rename with rollback.
- `DefragMode::InPlace`: Direct WAL-atomic modification of the existing image using round-based copy-on-write (COW) passes; directories and files are relocated into currently free blocks with metadata updates committed through the journal.

## Fragmentation analysis

Before and after defragmentation, [`DiskManager::analyze_fragmentation`](repo://src/disk/maintenance.rs#L137-L166) inspects the filesystem's `data_bitmap_block` using a read-only [`BitmapRef`](repo://src/bitmap.rs).

### 64-bit word scanning

Instead of checking bit by bit, the analyzer slices the bitmap into 8-byte chunks (`chunks_exact(8)`) and decodes them as little-endian 64-bit words via `u64::from_le_bytes` ([`analyze_fragmentation_internal`](repo://src/disk/maintenance.rs#L150-L255)):

- `word == 0`: All 64 data blocks are completely free. If not already tracking a free run, increments `free_runs` and extends `current_run_len` by 64.
- `word == u64::MAX`: All 64 blocks are fully allocated. Closes any open free run, recording `largest_free_run` and accumulating `total_gap_size`.
- Mixed word: Uses `word.count_ones()` to quickly tabulate allocated blocks, then iterates through each bit (`0..64`) with bitwise masks to track individual block boundaries and transitions.
- Trailing bits: Any leftover bits (`total_blocks % 64`) are checked at the end using `bitmap.get(i)` ([`analyze_fragmentation_internal`](repo://src/disk/maintenance.rs#L235-L250)).

### Metrics and fragmentation ratio

The resulting [`FragmentationStats`](repo://src/disk.rs#L157-L174) tracks:
- `total_blocks`, `used_blocks`, `free_blocks`
- `free_runs`: Number of separate contiguous sequences of free blocks
- `largest_free_run`: The size (in blocks) of the largest contiguous free chunk
- `avg_gap_size`: `total_gap_size / free_runs` (average size of free runs)
- `fragmentation_ratio`: Calculated as:

$$\text{fragmentation\_ratio} = \frac{\text{free\_runs} - 1}{\max(\text{free\_blocks} - 1, 1)}$$

If all free space forms a single contiguous run (`free_runs <= 1`), the ratio is `0.0` (optimal). If every free block is completely isolated (`free_runs == free_blocks`), the ratio approaches `1.0` (maximally fragmented).

## Safe defragmentation pipeline (out-of-place rebuild)

[`defragment_safe`](repo://src/disk/maintenance.rs#L484-L640) reorganizes the filesystem out-of-place to protect against crashes, power failures, or corruption. The process executes across six distinct stages:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant User
    participant DM as DiskManager
    participant Temp as Temp Image
    participant FS as Filesystem
    User->>DM: defragment(DefragMode::Safe)
    DM->>FS: fs::copy(source, .defrag.tmp)
    DM->>Temp: Open with preserved encryption key
    DM->>Temp: Scan inodes, preserve directory blocks
    DM->>Temp: Extract file data + compression/filter config
    DM->>Temp: Clear data bitmap (restore only dir blocks)
    DM->>Temp: Reallocate & rewrite files contiguously
    DM->>Temp: Flush
    DM->>FS: rename source -> .old
    DM->>FS: rename .defrag.tmp -> source
    DM->>Temp: Verify (open, fsck)
    alt Verification OK
        DM->>FS: unlink .old
        DM->>DM: reload_from_disk()
    else Verification Failed
        DM->>FS: rename .old -> source (rollback)
    end
```

### 1. Snapshot creation

The entire active image file is copied via `std::fs::copy(source_path, &temp_path)` ([`defragment_safe`](repo://src/disk/maintenance.rs#L498)). The destination defaults to `{source_path}.defrag.tmp` when no output path is provided. This guarantees that if the defragmentation process is killed mid-stream, the original image file remains untouched and uncorrupted.

### 2. Inode scan and metadata preservation

The temporary image is opened via `DiskManager::open_with_key(&temp_path, 0, enc_key)` ([`defragment_safe`](repo://src/disk/maintenance.rs#L501)), preserving the encryption key from the original image. Using [`BitmapRef::for_each_set_bit`](repo://src/bitmap.rs#L94-L108), all allocated inode indices are collected from `inode_bitmap_block` ([`defragment_safe`](repo://src/disk/maintenance.rs#L507-L512)):

- **Directories**: Directory blocks cannot simply be moved without updating parent pointer graphs, so directory block addresses are harvested via `collect_inode_blocks` and staged in `directory_blocks` ([`defragment_safe`](repo://src/disk/maintenance.rs#L514-L517)).
- **Regular Files**: For each file with `size > 0`, the file's exact compression status (`is_compressed = inode.compressed_size > 0`) and pre-compression filter configuration ([`FilterConfig`]: `typesize`, `delta`, `shuffle`, `bitshuffle`) are recorded ([`defragment_safe`](repo://src/disk/maintenance.rs#L519-L526)). **Seekable 64K chunked files** are detected by `INODE_FLAG_SEEKABLE_64K` and their `CompressionMode::Seekable` config is preserved.
- **Inode Reset**: The inode on disk is zeroed out (`size = 0`, `compressed_size = 0`, `blocks = [0; 12]`, `triple_indirect = 0`) via `write_inode` ([`defragment_safe`](repo://src/disk/maintenance.rs#L528-L534)), freeing the blocks for contiguous reassignment.

### 3. Bitmap reset

The entire data bitmap of the temporary image is wiped using `bitmap_slice.fill(0)` ([`defragment_safe`](repo://src/disk/maintenance.rs#L537)). Then, only the preserved directory block IDs (`directory_blocks`) are re-marked as allocated ([`defragment_safe`](repo://src/disk/maintenance.rs#L539-L545)). All other data blocks become completely free and unallocated.

### 4. Contiguous file rewrite

For each regular file, `write_data_with_filters` is invoked ([`defragment_safe`](repo://src/disk/maintenance.rs#L557)):
- Because the data bitmap was cleared and allocation starts from `data_block_start` using sequential hint-based allocation, each file receives a strictly contiguous sequence of data blocks.
- The original compression setting (`CompressionMode::Always` if previously compressed, `CompressionMode::Seekable` for chunked files, else `CompressionMode::Never`) and filter configuration are reapplied, preserving space efficiency without altering compression/filter semantics.
- Bytes moved and files processed counters are updated for final reporting.

### 5. Durability flush

`temp_dm.flush()` commits all dirty pages and metadata to disk, and the temporary `DiskManager` handle is explicitly dropped to release memory maps and file descriptors ([`defragment_safe`](repo://src/disk/maintenance.rs#L560-L561)).

### 6. Transactional 3-step atomic rename

The replacement uses a crash-safe three-step rename protocol ([`defragment_safe`](repo://src/disk/maintenance.rs#L563-L605)):

1. `rename(source_path, source_path.old)` — original becomes backup
2. `rename(temp_path, source_path)` — new defragged image becomes active
3. Verify by opening the new image and running `verify_integrity()` (fsck)

**Rollback on failure**: If either rename fails, or verification fails (fsck not clean, or cannot open), the backup `.old` is renamed back to `source_path`, restoring the original image atomically. On success, the `.old` backup is deleted and the active `DiskManager` handle is live-reloaded via `reload_from_disk()` to synchronize with the new file.

## In-place defragmentation (WAL-atomic COW)

[`defragment_inplace`](repo://src/disk/maintenance.rs#L643-L735) directly compacts and reorganizes physical data blocks within the existing image without allocating duplicate temporary files. It operates in two variants depending on whether the image has journaling enabled.

### Common phases (both variants)

1. **Fragmentation analysis** — captures `stats_before` via `analyze_fragmentation_internal`.
2. **Short-circuit** — if already perfectly compacted (`free_runs == 1` and final block is free), returns zero-work `DefragStats`.
3. **Inode collection** — single pass collects all allocated inodes into `dir_inodes`, `file_inodes`, `other_inodes` without thrashing `inode_cache` ([`defragment_inplace_on`](repo://src/disk/maintenance.rs#L660-L685)).
4. **Journal quiesce (journaled only)** — drains pending async ranges, flushes mmap, checkpoints WAL to head so the ring is clean ([`defragment_inplace_on`](repo://src/disk/maintenance.rs#L687-L698)).
5. **Defragmentation core** — dispatches to either `defragment_inplace_journaled_cow` or `defragment_inplace_legacy` ([`defragment_inplace_on`](repo://src/disk/maintenance.rs#L700-L725)).
6. **Post-defrag verification** — runs `verify_integrity`; fails the operation if not clean.

### Legacy (non-journaled) in-place defragmentation

[`defragment_inplace_legacy`](repo://src/disk/maintenance.rs#L754-L975) uses a cycle-aware block permutation algorithm:

1. **Target layout planning** — computes contiguous target locations for all blocks (`old_to_new` map) starting from `data_block_start`. Directories first, then regular files (including `ChunkEntry` runs expanded to individual blocks), then indirect blocks (SIB, DIB, TIB).
2. **ChunkEntry handling** — for seekable 64K files, `collect_inode_block_layout` expands packed `ChunkEntry` values into their constituent contiguous block runs ([`collect_inode_block_layout`](repo://src/disk/maintenance.rs#L170-L200)). A parallel `old_entry_to_new` map rewrites the packed pointer values after permutation.
3. **Cycle-aware permutation** — moves blocks using a scratch buffer only when cycles are detected; free targets are consumed first to avoid unnecessary copies ([`defragment_inplace_legacy`](repo://src/disk/maintenance.rs#L900-L960)).
4. **Pointer updates** — inode direct/SIB/DIB/TIB slots and indirect block pointer tables are rewritten to new locations via `lookup_new` ([`defragment_inplace_legacy`](repo://src/disk/maintenance.rs#L962-L1010)).
5. **Bitmap rebuild** — data bitmap is cleared and `set_range(0, total_used)` marks the new contiguous prefix as allocated ([`defragment_inplace_legacy`](repo://src/disk/maintenance.rs#L1012-L1020)).
6. **Hints & cache remap** — `free_block_hint` updated; `ShardedDirCache` entries remapped in place; payload caches cleared ([`defragment_inplace_legacy`](repo://src/disk/maintenance.rs#L1022-L1030)).

### Journaled in-place defragmentation (round-based COW)

[`defragment_inplace_journaled_cow`](repo://src/disk/maintenance.rs#L977-L1255) is a fully WAL-atomic, round-based copy-on-write algorithm designed to never lose data even on mid-round crashes.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant DM as DiskManagerInner
    participant WAL as Journal Ring
    participant Bitmap as Alloc Bitmap (in-mem)
    loop Each Round
        DM->>Bitmap: Select units whose targets are currently free
        DM->>DM: Copy payload blocks to free destinations (memcpy)
        DM->>DM: Flush destination ranges (Strict mode)
        DM->>WAL: Stage metadata ops (inode updates, bitmap alloc/free, indirect ptrs)
        DM->>WAL: Commit single bounded transaction (fits in 1/2 ring)
        DM->>WAL: apply_journal_ops (in-place metadata apply)
        DM->>Bitmap: Update in-mem alloc bitmap (clear src, set dst)
        DM->>DM: Sync metadata ranges per DurabilityMode
        DM->>WAL: Checkpoint (retire WAL ring before next round)
    end
    DM->>DM: Update free_block_hint, remap dir cache, clear payload caches
```

#### Data structures

- **`RelocUnit`**: Describes one contiguous relocation (payload run or indirect block). Fields: `curr_start`, `block_count`, `target_start`, `owner` (enum: `InodeDirect`, `InodeSib`, `InodeDib`, `InodeTib`, `IndirectSlot`), optional `chunk_entry` (for seekable files), optional `self_ind_idx` (if this unit is itself an indirect block).
- **`UnitOwner`**: Traces each unit back to its owning inode slot or indirect block entry, enabling precise metadata updates.
- **In-memory allocation mirror** (`alloc_bm_bytes`): Compact byte vector mirroring the on-disk data bitmap, updated each round to track which blocks are free for subsequent rounds.

#### Round execution

1. **Batch selection** — Greedily picks a set of pending units whose `target_start..target_start+block_count` are free in `alloc_bm_bytes` and whose estimated WAL transaction size fits within half the journal ring (`max_payload_per_tx`) ([`defragment_inplace_journaled_cow`](repo://src/disk/maintenance.rs#L1095-L1135)).
2. **Cycle breaker** — If no units have free targets (all targets occupied by other pending units), picks the smallest blocking unit and moves it to a high-address free scratch run found by reverse-scan ([`find_free_run_high_to_low`](repo://src/disk/maintenance.rs#L1080-L1093)).
3. **Payload copy & flush** — `mmap.copy_within` copies source blocks to destinations; in `Strict` durability mode, destination ranges are flushed via `flush_range` before WAL commit ([`defragment_inplace_journaled_cow`](repo://src/disk/maintenance.rs#L1137-L1155)).
4. **WAL staging** — Builds a transaction containing:
